motivation: Current-state oracle removes the sensing problem. Test whether recovery notice helps an actual causal controller by avoiding probe reservations or restoring nominal pilot promptly.
world: Unchanged C2 six-vehicle synthetic exogenous-acceptance model; not a learned physical response
causal_candidates: exponential failed-probe backoff 1 to 2 to 4 slots
selection: One global causal policy selected by development mean delivered kWh; freeze before evaluating seeds 400-419
oracle_contract: Same selected EDF and only past commands/actual response. A recovery notice can be used only after positive pilot produced zero current. No current-state oracle, no notice of future pause onset. Exact recovery notices become available 15 minutes before recovery or throughout the observed pause. A known future recovery stops probes before ETA and restores nominal eligibility at ETA.
controls: Include selected causal probe policy, original every-slot probe EDF, current-state MPC and full-information offline optimum; no-pause control on the same seed/capacity pairs
metrics: Paired delivered kWh, wasted reservation, total shortfall, fully served sessions, runtime, capacity and energy checks; bootstrap 2000 times by seed
limits: Perfect notification is not an implemented predictor and fixed-policy oracle is not a universal information upper bound. Test whether a mechanism has conditional opportunity, not production effectiveness or novelty. No retuning from evaluation outcomes.
change: P1 exposed artificial throttling with abundant feeder capacity. Add the same causal spare-budget fill to every controller: after active/probe allocations, allocate residual feeder budget up to connected unmet sessions nominal rates. No future input is used. Re-select on development and evaluate fresh seeds 500-519. Preserve P1 diagnostics.
additional_check: At 180A all causal and notice controllers must match the offline bound, because all six nominal pilots fit simultaneously.
